chapter_seo_title: Dao Guai Yi Xian Ch. 497: Li Huowang Discovers Zhuge Yuan's Remains Forged into a Sword
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang spots a bone-sword made from Zhuge Yuan's spinal cord in the hands of the new Chief Recorder. His decision is instant: he's taking it back.
og_title: Dao Guai Yi Xian Ch. 497: Zhuge Yuan's Sword
og_description: The Office didn't just keep Zhuge Yuan's gear—they refined his spine into a blade. Li Huowang's quiet fury is terrifying.
twitter_title: Ch. 497: A Sword Made of a Friend
twitter_description: Li Huowang sees Zhuge Yuan's remains wielded as a weapon. He doesn't hesitate. He's going to take it back.

lore_anchors.definition: A metal writing-stylus weapon used in wuxia; named after King Yama's judge. Zhuge Yuan's personal weapon, now wielded by an Office Daoist.
An even rarer constitution than Heart-Element; a person whose reality-anchoring nature can be refined into artifacts. Zhuge Yuan was one.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office; the position is both bureaucratic and supernatural.
A cult worshipping Yú'er Shén (Child-God); being cleared out by the Office in this chapter.
A deity from the *Classic of Mountains and Seas* with a human head and two serpent bodies; worshipped by the Dharma Sect.
A folk figure who loans knives and later collects the borrower's luck; Hong Da brought Li Huowang into the Office.
A government body monitoring supernatural activity; struggling to hold back the Heavenly Calamity.
A Daoist/Buddhist term for the mortal body as an impermanent vessel; Zhuge Yuan uses it to dismiss his own remains.

cultural_notes_faq.a: A martial weapon shaped like a writing brush, used to strike pressure points. In mythology, it belongs to King Yama's judge. Zhuge Yuan's personal weapon is now in Office hands.
It opens a rift to the alternate history of Great Qi. When the rift closes, anything caught in it is cut across the boundary between two worlds, effectively slicing the target into pieces.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang so determined to get it back?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Zhuge Yuan died for him. Abandoning his remains to be used as a weapon is something Li Huowang cannot accept, no matter how tactically unwise the rescue might be.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the new Chief Recorder?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A purple-lipped woman, the current leader of the Office team. She wields the bone-sword made from Zhuge Yuan's spinal cord.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Zhuge Yuan's ghost in this chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes, Li Huowang's hallucination of Zhuge Yuan is present. He advises Li Huowang to let it go, saying it is just a "stinking bag of skin."
